definitions.explanation: A style of handwriting in which letters are joined together in a flowing manner. Most commonly refers to cursive Latin alphabet writing, but can also refer to cursive styles of other scripts.

examples.japanese: {筆記体|ひっきたい}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{名前|なまえ}→名前：02234_namae⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{書|か}く→書く：00477_kaku⟧。
examples.english: To write one's name in cursive.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{手紙|てがみ}→手紙：00675_tegami⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{筆記体|ひっきたい}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{書|か}かれていて→書く：00477_kaku⟧⟦{読|よ}み→読む：00426_yomu⟧にくい。
examples.english: This letter is written in cursive and is hard to read.

examples.japanese: ⟦{最近|さいきん}→最近：00881_saikin⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{筆記体|ひっきたい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{習|なら}わない→習う：00479_narau⟧⟦{学校|がっこう}→学校：00055_gakkou⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{増|ふ}えている→増える：01183_fueru⟧。
examples.english: Recently, more and more schools no longer teach cursive writing.

notes:
A compound of ⟦{筆記|ひっき}→筆記：00101_hikki⟧ (writing) and ⟦{体|たい}→体：09872_tai⟧ (style/form). In Japanese education, {筆記体|ひっきたい} usually refers to cursive Latin alphabet writing, which was once widely taught in English classes but is now less common.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {筆記体|ひっきたい}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{書|か}く→書く：00477_kaku⟧: to write in cursive
- {筆記体|ひっきたい}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{読|よ}めない→読む：00426_yomu⟧: cannot read cursive
- {筆記体|ひっきたい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{練習|れんしゅう}→練習：05323_renshuu⟧: cursive writing practice

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {活字体|かつじたい}: print style; block letters — the non-cursive counterpart
- ⟦{草書|そうしょ}→草書：19196_sousho⟧: cursive-style kanji — the highly simplified, flowing style of writing kanji
- ⟦{行書|ぎょうしょ}→行書：19195_gyousho⟧: semi-cursive kanji — an intermediate style between block and cursive kanji
- ⟦ブロック→ブロック：05902_burokku⟧⟦{体|たい}→体：09872_tai⟧: block letters — print-style alphabet writing
